source.title: An update on Weihrauch complexity, and some open questions

accepted.question_text: Consider the algebraic structure of the Weihrauch degrees with constants 0, 1, and ⊤, binary operations ⊓, ⊔, ×, ⋆, and →, and unary operations *, b, and ⋄, where 0, 1, and ⊤ represent the vacuously true, the true, and the false degree respectively; ⊓ is the ‘or’ operation; ⊓, ×, and ⋆ are additive, multiplicative, and sequential forms of conjunction; → is the right residual of ⋆; * gives access to finitely many parallel instances; b gives access to countably many parallel instances; and ⋄ gives access to finitely many consecutive instances. What can be said about the first-order theory of this algebraic structure, and in particular is its quantifier-free fragment finitely axiomatizable? More generally, what can be said about the corresponding theories obtained by restricting to fragments of this signature?

evidence.quote: In logical terms, the algebraic structure of the Weihrauch degrees is (W; 0, 1, ⊤;⊓,⊔, ×, ⋆,→, ∗, b, ⋄), with the constants 0, 1, ⊤ being vacuously true, true and false respectively. The ⊓-operator is or, and ⊓, ×, ⋆ are all logical ands, the additive, multiplicative and sequential and respectively. The right-residual to ⋆ is →, we do not have additional implications. The unary “bang” operators ∗, b, ⋄ provide access to finitely many parallel instances, countably-many parallel instances and finitely-many consecutive instances.
Open Question 2. What can we say about Th(W; 0, 1, ⊤;⊓,⊔, ×, ⋆,→, ∗, b, ⋄)? Is its quantifier-free part finitely axiomatisable? What about fragments of the signature?

accepted.question_text: Within the Weihrauch-degree structure whose operations include ×, ⋆, →, *, b, and ⋄, is the countable-parallelization operator b definable from the remaining operations and order-theoretic structure?

evidence.quote: The unary “bang” operators ∗, b, ⋄ provide access to finitely many parallel instances, countably-many parallel instances and finitely-many consecutive instances.

Another line of questions concerns definability of operators from others. As supremum and infimum, we know ⊔ and ⊓ to be definable in terms of ≤W. It is easy to see that ∗ is definable from 1, ≤W and ×, in very much the same way that Westrick’s result has shown ⋄ to be definable from 1, ≤W and ⋆. By definition, → is definable from ⋆ and ≤W. What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure?

accepted.question_text: Let overt choice for a space X be the computational problem that receives overt (positive) information about a closed subset of X and must output a point in that set. For spaces X that are non-Fréchet-Urysohn and coPolish, can the Weihrauch degree of overt choice be determined more precisely than the currently known bounds LPO ≤W VC_X ≤W (isEmpty : A(N^N) → S)?
accepted.context_brief: Overt choice on non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces

evidence.quote: One such example is found in overt choice for incomplete countably-based spaces. This principle is given overt (aka positive) information about a closed subset, and needs to output a point in this set.

For overt choice VCX for non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces X we only know that LPO ≤W VCX ≤W (isEmpty : A(NN) → S) – which is perfectly compatible with VCX being a familiar Weihrauch degree, and is a remarkably weak classification.
Open Question 4 (de Brecht, Schröder & P. [9]). Can we classify overt choice for non-Fréchet-Urysohn coPolish spaces more precisely?

accepted.question_text: Is there a naturally arising computational problem, for example one coming from linear algebra, whose Weihrauch degree is exactly AoUC^⋄, where AoUC is the problem of finding a solution x to the equation b x = a under the condition 0 ≤ a ≤ b and ⋄ denotes the operation giving finitely many consecutive instances?
accepted.context_brief: Natural examples of the AoUC^⋄ degree

evidence.quote: The unary “bang” operators ∗, b, ⋄ provide access to finitely many parallel instances, countably-many parallel instances and finitely-many consecutive instances.
Let AoUC be the degree of finding a solution to bx = a where 0 ≤ a ≤ b
Open Question 14. Is there any natural problem (e.g. from linear algebra) in the Weihrauch degree AoUC⋄?

accepted.question_text: Extended Weihrauch degrees are an enlargement of the usual Weihrauch degrees that also includes representatives of false theorems. Is there a clear general description of how the new degrees that appear in this extended setting are positioned relative to the ordinary Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: Bauer and Yoshimura introduced the notion of instance reducibility, a special case of which are the extended Weihrauch degrees (which include representatives of false theorems, too).
Open Question 19. Is there a clear picture of how the additional degrees in the extended Weihrauch degrees relate to the Weihrauch degrees?

accepted.question_text: Extended Weihrauch degrees include examples coming from false statements, while the usual Weihrauch lattice is often organized around a familiar scaffold of benchmark degrees such as closed choice principles and levels of the effective Baire hierarchy. What are interesting examples of extended Weihrauch degrees arising from false statements, and how do those examples compare with those familiar benchmark Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: There is a canonic scaffold of familiar degrees in the Weihrauch lattice, the closed choice principles and the levels of the effective Baire hierarchy, which has served well for many classifications of computational problems.
Bauer and Yoshimura introduced the notion of instance reducibility, a special case of which are the extended Weihrauch degrees (which include representatives of false theorems, too).
Open Question 20. What are some examples of interesting extended Weihrauch degrees of false statements, and how do they relate to the usual scaffolding Weihrauch degrees?

needs_review.question_text_raw: What about the jump of Weihrauch degrees (cf. [6])?

evidence.quote: What other definability results can we obtain? In particular, is b definable from the rest of the structure? What about the jump of Weihrauch degrees (cf. [6])?
Another example for this is found in the principle DS that takes as input a linear order with a descending sequence, and then finds such a sequence.
Open Question 6. Does C′ {0,1} N ≤W DS hold?
Let NON : {0, 1} N ⇒ {0, 1} N be defined as q ∈ NON(p) iff q is not computable relative to p.
Open Question 8. Does NON × LLPO ≤W RT2 2 hold?

needs_review.question_text_raw: Is there a square-root operator on the Weihrauch degrees?

evidence.quote: Open Question 12. Is there a square-root operator on the Weihrauch degrees?
let List{0,1} N be the problem “given a countable closed subset of Cantor space, find an enumeration of its elements”.
Open Question 13. Does List{0,1} N ⋆ List{0,1} N ≡W UCNN hold?

needs_review.question_text_raw: What is the relationship between Det^1_2 and PTT^1_2?

evidence.quote: but the following remains open (see [27] for definitions): Open Question 16. What is the relationship between Det2 and PTT2?
Open Question 17 (Marcone & Valenti [34, Question 6.2]). Does Σ0 1−RT ≤W CNN hold?

needs_review.question_text_raw: What is the Weihrauch degree of obtaining a point of discontinuity of a function from a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for it?

evidence.quote: Open Question 18 (Nobrega & P. [35]). What is the Weihrauch degree of obtaining a point of discontinuity of a function from a Player I winning strategy in the Wadge game for it?
It is known that a computable winning strategy implies the existence of a computable point of discontinuity, but not whether there is a uniform argument to establish this.
